title: SelPE: Progressive Selection for Private Structured Text Synthesis

problem.claim: Privacy-sensitive domains have limited access to structured textual records, constraining model development and analysis.

gap.claim: Existing differential privacy synthesis methods either fail to model free-form text faithfully or fail to preserve structural constraints.

contributions.claim: SelPE presents a selection-guided progressive-evolution approach for privately synthesizing structured text from small samples.

SelPE uses multi-batch top-1 selections for privacy-budget allocation, a two-stage semantic-abstraction and schema-realization pipeline, and a multi-channel distance kernel over textual, categorical, and numeric fields.
A non-private contrastive expansion mechanism promotes diversity without additional privacy cost.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that SelPE consistently improves structural validity, fidelity, and downstream utility under strict differential privacy budgets.
The authors report that the improvements are particularly pronounced in low-data regimes.

narrative_sequence.summary: Structured textual records support downstream learning and decision-making.
Privacy regulation leaves few private examples available for development and analysis.
Existing private synthesis methods do not jointly handle free-form text and structural constraints.
SelPE combines progressive selection, staged generation, native-representation distance modeling, and contrastive expansion.
The authors report improved validity, fidelity, and downstream utility under strict privacy budgets, especially with little data.

source_observation.claim: The method separates semantic abstraction from schema realization and evaluates mixed field types in their native representations.

interpretation.claim: Separating meaning from schema construction may help preserve both textual content and structural validity in heterogeneous records.

application.claim: For structured text generation, consider staged generation with field-type-aware evaluation rather than a single undifferentiated generation step.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this decomposition benefits datasets or schemas outside the reported setting.

source_observation.claim: The approach concentrates privacy budget on sequential top-1 selections instead of noisy aggregation or private model training.

interpretation.claim: Under tight privacy constraints, selective guidance may be more efficient than privatizing every aggregation or training operation.

application.claim: When privacy budgets are limited, investigate selective mechanisms that allocate privacy expenditure to high-impact guidance decisions.

exception.claim: The abstract does not provide the privacy accounting, selection error behavior, or conditions under which this strategy is preferable.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, sample sizes, privacy parameters, baselines, or metric values.
The abstract does not describe the experimental protocol or independent verification of the reported improvements.
The abstract does not establish reproducibility, generalization beyond the evaluated low-data regimes, or computational costs.
